title: In 1977, Lava Raced Down a Volcano at 40 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: Lava can outrun you. In 1977, it hit forty miles an hour.
Mount Nyiragongo in the Congo cracked open on January tenth.
It held a lake of molten rock. It drained in under an hour.
That lava poured down the slopes faster than a car on a city street.
Most lava is thick and slow. This was runny, like hot water.
Forty miles an hour. Faster than you can run.

description:
On 10 January 1977 Mount Nyiragongo in the Democratic Republic of the Congo erupted and sent lava racing down its slopes at up to 40 miles an hour.
The volcano's lava lake drained in under an hour. Its lava is unusually runny, which lets it flow far faster than most.
Could you outrun lava? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: Nyiragongo has one of the largest lava lakes on Earth and it erupted again in 2002 and 2021. Would you hike to the crater?
